set.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: the introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source, read against Donaldson's Question 3 and Fine-Yao Conjecture 1.1; the theorem states the full normalized deformation with all three classes fixed and a hyperkahler endpoint, and the paper says it resolves that conjecture. The proof was not refereed. It does not go through the hypersymplectic flow; convergence or uniqueness of that flow is left open. Key inputs are Bauer's bound for symplectic four-manifolds with torsion first Chern class, Preiss's rectifiability theorem, Riviere-Tian regularity of integral cycles, and the companion release paper Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds (itself unreviewed), whose needed proofs are reproduced in Sections 3 and 4. The October 7 edition leaves Theorem 1.1 unchanged; it drops the citation of Li-Zhang's comparison of taming and compatible cones and obtains the prescribed taming class from the paper's own class criterion (under its definite-pair and $b^+=3$ hypotheses), so it does not rely on the general cone equality that the revised Taming paper narrowed. No Lean formalization is supplied for this family.

why: Source revised (Oct 6): Theorem 1.1 unchanged; cone corollary narrowed to h_J^- = b2+ - 1 with a strict-inclusion example; resultNote corrected

set.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if a smooth almost complex structure $J$ on a closed connected smooth four-manifold is tamed by a symplectic form, there is a smooth symplectic form compatible with the same $J$. The October 6 edition corrects the cone corollary of the first edition, which had claimed $\mathcal K_J^t=\mathcal K_J^c+H_J^-$ in general via Li-Zhang: it now characterizes the compatible cone by strict intersection positivity on the closure of the invariant part of the taming cone, proves that equality only when $h_J^-=b_2^+-1$ (so when $b_2^+=1$ every taming class still contains a compatible form), and gives a four-torus example where the inclusion is strict. Not shown: that an arbitrary taming class contains a compatible form, anything in dimensions above four, or Donaldson's separate a priori estimate conjecture for the prescribed-volume equation.
set.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: abstract, introduction and Theorem 1.1 of the TeX source, read against Donaldson's question as cited; the October 6 edition leaves Theorem 1.1 unchanged and revises only the cone corollary (see the result note), so the headline and the Candidate rating stand. Lean-checked on the release's Comparator challenge TamingCompatibility (declaration OAI.TamingCompatibility.taming_implies_compatibility, listed in lean/formalization.yaml). Its statement was read here: for a compact connected Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold modelled on R^4 and a smooth almost complex structure $J$ with $J^2=-1$, if some symplectic two-form tames $J$ then some symplectic two-form tames $J$ and is $J$-invariant. Two-forms, smoothness and closedness are encoded by hand through pullbacks along smooth chart maps rather than Mathlib's differential forms; that encoding was read but not audited in depth. It states the headline claim, with the same $J$ and no cohomology class prescribed. Not rebuilt here. The Lean file is unchanged at the new commit; lean/formalization.yaml still lists the September 23 manuscript.
